Subject: MAP: pen test handoff, vuln triage SLA & supplier questionnaire

Hi Sara / Tom —

Great to meet you on the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth in the MAP:

- Redwood asks: receipt of the latest penetration test (redacted okay) + CSV of findings where possible.
- Compliance check: please confirm SOC 2 status (Type I/II, date) and whether GDPR/HIPAA scope applies to the integration.
- Questionnaire kickoff: attaching a short vendor security questionnaire (MAP includes the link) — if you prefer we can initiate a DocuSign VDA first.
- Triage SLA proposal (we can adjust): Critical: 3 business days acknowledgement / 5 business days initial triage; High: 5 days acknowledgement / 10 days triage; Medium/Low per monthly cadence.
- Scan cadence & retest: recommend a 30-day retest window for critical items, 60–90 days for high. Confirm if you run continuous scanning or periodics.

Attachments: MAP_ProspectCo_v0.3.xlsx (draft) — please review and let us know which redaction level for your pen report (full, redacted PII, or summary only). Also let us know preferred delivery (SFTP / secure share / presigned s3).

Next actions I’ll take: fold your answers into the MAP and loop in Karthik (security) for technical intake. Please reply with the preferred transfer method and an approximate date you can share the report.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

Subject: Re: MAP: pen test handoff, vuln triage SLA & supplier questionnaire

Thanks Rachel — good call. A few quick data points from our side: 

- SOC 2: In progress (Type II target completion March 2028); we have Type I from 2026 on file.
- GDPR/HIPAA: ProspectCo handles PHI in one workflow; HIPAA will apply for that scope.
- Scanning cadence: we run quarterly authenticated scans and continuous SCA; we can provide a consolidated CSV export.
- Pen test delivery: our security team prefers redacted PDF + findings CSV over SFTP. We need to redact client-identifying PII before sending.

We can provide the redacted pen-test by EOD next Tuesday (2027-12-07). On the VDA / disclosure agreement: we have a standard NDA in place with Redwood, but if you require a VDA we can sign it — please share the DocuSign link.

Tom and I will prepare the files. Thanks for the SLA proposals — we’ll review and flag any constraints.

—Sara

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@prospectco.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2027 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood vuln ops & evidence intake — confirmation of requirements

Hi Sara / team —

Karthik here (Head of Security Ops at Redwood). Thanks for the quick turnaround on this. A few specifics to make intake straightforward on both sides: 

1) Required deliverables for efficient triage: redacted PDF of the pen-test report + machine-readable findings (CSV) with columns for: finding id, title, severity (CVSS if available), vector, affected component, recommended remediation, reproducible steps.

2) Transfer method: presigned S3 link works fine (we can generate and expire in 7 days) or a secure file drop. If you prefer SFTP, we can provide details. For PGP we can accept a signed upload; tell us which you prefer.

3) SLA & triage flow (confirmed):
   - Acknowledgement: within 24 business hours of file receipt.
   - Initial classification and assignment: within 3 business days for Critical items, 7 business days for High.
   - Triage notes: we will create tickets in our tracking system and share a triage CSV export.

4) Retest workflow: we can validate fixes in staging. For critical issues we’ll request evidence (retest scan or PoC) and perform verification within 5 business days of receiving retest evidence.

5) Disclosure / coordinated release: Redwood’s standard approach is coordinated disclosure — we won’t publicize findings and will give you 30 days to remediate critical items before any external reporting unless there is active exploitation. We’ll sign a VDA if needed.

I’ve attached our Vuln_SLA_and_Process_v2.pdf for your legal/security teams to review. I’ll follow up once we see your upload and will open triage tickets.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head, Security Ops | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
[Attachment: Vuln_SLA_and_Process_v2.pdf (pdf)]

Tom / Sara — confirmed receipt of the redacted report and CSV via your presigned link. Appreciate the clear summary. Next steps from Redwood: 

1) Acknowledged and created MAP entry (RDW-2391). I’ve asked Marissa to own scheduling and ensure the MAP milestones reflect the remediations dates you shared.
2) Karthik will open triage tickets for the Critical and High items and assign owners; we’ll share a triage CSV within 48 hours. Karthik: can you confirm whether we need an executed VDA before we access the full CSV?
3) Our proposed validation cadence: we’ll run a focused retest in staging as soon as you indicate fixes are deployed. For the critical auth bypass we’ll prioritize verification within 5 business days of your retest evidence.
4) I’m attaching a one-page MAP update and a DocuSign link for the Vulnerability Disclosure Agreement — if your security legal prefers, sign and we’ll countersign.

Please mark the MAP with the remediation ETA for the critical fix (12/10) and share any retest timeframe you prefer. We’ll keep communications limited to this thread for traceability.

Thanks again — and welcome aboard. Looking forward to closing this out quickly.

Rachel Kim
